parcalar.metin: [excited, emphatic science storyteller] This is Hoover Dam, and the lake behind it is basically a giant battery! Energy Sources, episode three: water.
This energy also comes from the sun. The sun evaporates water, clouds drop rain and snow on the mountains, and rivers flow downhill.
Hoover is a concrete arch-gravity dam, two hundred twenty-one metres tall. It's over two hundred metres thick at the base. The higher the water falls from, the more energy it carries.
Water rushes down giant steel penstocks, nine metres across, and slams into the turbines.
Inside each turbine, the runner spins, and a generator on the same shaft turns that rotation into electricity.
Seventeen generators were built for about two thousand eighty megawatts. But after years of drought, Lake Mead has dropped, and by 2021 the dam's capacity had fallen by about a quarter.
Some plants pump water up to a higher lake when electricity is plentiful, and release it when it's needed. A true giant battery!
The world's largest is China's Three Gorges Dam, with more than twenty-two thousand megawatts of installed capacity.
[excited] From rain to electricity! Next episode: the power of the atom. Follow Kozmos Lab.
